claim.claim-text: a steerable sheath (1102, 1702) having a distal steerable portion (1008); a medical device (1010, 1704); and a handle assembly (1002, 1703) comprising: a handle body (1007, 1705); and a first actuator (1001, 1720) adapted to be actuated relative to the handle body to cause deflection of the distal steerable portion, and
wherein the handle assembly is configured to be actuated to cause movement of the medical device relative to the steerable sheath.
2. The tool of claim 1, wherein the handle assembly is in operable communication with the steerable sheath and the medical device.

3. The tool of claim 1 or claim 2, wherein the distal steerable region is in operable communication with at least one pull wire (1104), wherein the first actuator is in operable communication with the at least one pull wire such that actuation of the first actuator relative to the handle body causes the deflection of the distal steerable portion.

4. The tool of any preceding claim, wherein the first actuator is adapted to be rotated relative to the handle body such that rotation of the first actuator relative to the handle body causes the deflection of the distal steerable region.

5. The tool of any preceding claim, wherein the medical device comprises an elongate medical tool with a distal portion that comprises a working end, wherein at least a portion of the elongate medical tool is disposed within the steerable sheath, optionally wherein the elongate medical tool is configured such that deflection of the distal steerable portion causes deflection of the elongate medical tool.

6. The tool of any preceding claim, wherein the handle assembly further comprises a second actuator (1003, 1780) adapted to be actuated relative to the handle body to cause rotation of the medical device relative to the steerable sheath.
7. The tool of claim 6, wherein the second actuator is adapted to be rotated relative to the handle body and is also adapted to be moved axially relative to the handle body.

8. The tool of claim 7, wherein the second actuator is in operable communication with the elongate medical tool such that axial movement of the second actuator relative to the handle body causes axial movement of the elongate medical tool relative to a distal end of the steerable sheath, and such that rotation of the second actuator relative to the handle body causes rotation of the elongate medical tool relative to the distal end of the steerable sheath.

9. The tool of any one of claims 6-8, wherein the second actuator is configured to interface with the handle assembly such that the interface with the handle assembly restricts at least one of: axial movement of the second actuator in both the proximal and distal directions within a fixed range of motion, and rotational movement of the second actuator in both directions of rotation within a fixed range of motion.

10. The tool of any preceding claim, wherein the handle assembly further comprises a third actuator (1005) adapted to be actuated relative to the handle body to cause axial movement of the medical device relative to the steerable sheath.

11. The tool of any preceding claim, wherein the steerable sheath comprises a proximal portion (1006) that is configured not to bend significantly when the distal steerable portion is steered, optionally wherein the distal steerable portion is constructed from a softer or less rigid material and/or composite construction than the proximal portion.
12. The tool of any preceding claim, wherein the medical device comprises an ultrasound probe.
13. The tool of any preceding claim, wherein the medical tool comprises a tool lock (1755).

14. The tool of claim 13, wherein the tool lock is contained within the handle assembly and is coupled to the second actuator, optionally wherein the tool lock and the second actuator engage one another magnetically.
15. The tool of claim 13 or claim 14, wherein the tool lock is configured to limit axial and rotational movement of the medical device relative to the steerable sheath within fixed ranges of motion.
